column9:
If things don't go to plan, there are a few options. 
The units can always be rented if they do not sell.
The units can be sold for less and investors will receive a smaller return.
Limited partners can sell their shares if they need to liquidate.
We can refinance the building and change to rentals. The refinance could potentially return all of the investors investment and provide some cash flow.
column11:
As units sell the waterfall is as follows:
Repay debt (Anticipated to be around $100M)
Repay Pref Equity ($5.0M)
Repay LP investment ($18M)
Pay LP pref (12% accrued, paid from deal profit)
Pay LP profit (remaining after the pref above)

column13: The construction loan will be around 7.15% over the 30 day SOFR rate which today puts it just over 10%. We will also be buying a cap which means that the rate won't go over the max rate we set which will most likely be 11%. So in layman's terms, the most the rate can go is 11% and if rates begin to recede next year (which we believe they will), we will benefit from a lower rate than the current one.
